chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Dawud ibn Zurbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

You place your hand upon the place where the pain is, and you say three times: 'Allah, Allah is my Lord truly. I do not associate anything with Him. O Allah, You are (the relief) for it and for all great troubles, so relieve it from me.'

key_terms.لَا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئاً: I do not associate anything with Him (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and method for relieving physical pain according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith outlines a tactile supplication where the believer places their hand on the site of pain while reciting a declaration of pure monotheism (Tawhid) to seek relief. It reflects the Shia tradition of combining physical action with spiritual invocation, emphasizing that Allah is the ultimate source of healing for all ailments. This practice underscores the belief that divine mercy is accessible through sincere reliance on God alone, without associating partners with Him.
